articles.title: How Netflix and the NFL Hope to Establish New Thanksgiving Eve Tradition With Game and U2 Half-Time Show: ‘We Want to Create Those Global Water Cooler Moments’
articles.summary: Thanksgiving Day has sported NFL games since the league’s inception in 1920, and now Turkey Day tussles on the gridiron are supercharged for the streaming future. On Nov. 25, Netflix and the NFL would like football fans to join them for a new holiday tradition: the Thanksgiving Eve game.
body: “As the NFL opened up more inventory and started talking to us about [possibly adding] more games, [Thanksgiving Eve] is one that they mentioned and immediately it felt like the perfect fit,” says Spitzer, who spoke with Variety while sporting a New England Patriots cap.

Onnie Bose, the NFL’s VP of broadcasting, echoes that sentiment. The league has learned “over the last few years that when family and friends are together, they gravitate toward watching our games,” Bose says. “Our Thanksgiving viewership has always been strong. I think it’s exploded. We hit 57 million viewers with the Kansas City-Dallas game last year.”

There is precedent for staking out new NFL-watching traditions, as the league has worked closely with Amazon Prime Video over the last few years to successfully establish the Black Friday game on the day after Thanksgiving.

“We’ve been building Black Friday with Amazon over the last few years. So Thanksgiving is a clear natural weekend where people are together,” Bose says. “They’re watching football. We’ve seen that on Christmas also in the last few years. We just looked at it as an opportunity to do something new.”

articles.title: Kevin Kline Reunites With Meryl Streep in ‘The Corrections’ Series at Netflix
articles.summary: Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the Netflix limited series adaptation of “The Corrections,” Variety has learned. Based on the novel of the same name by Jonathan Franzen, the series was originally announced with Streep attached back in April.
body: Kline will star as Alfred Lambert, who is described as “a once-powerful patriarch who is battling the afflictions of aging. A man of strict principles and old-fashioned decorum, Alfred must come to terms with his three very modern children—a daughter whose secrets he can no longer protect, an older son who has displaced him as the authority in the family, and a wayward son whose forgiveness he yearns for.”

The casting marks the latest collaboration between Kline and Streep. The two most famously worked together in the hit 1982 drama “Sophie’s Choice,” which was Kline’s feature debut and for which Streep earned her second Academy Award. Kline and Streep have also appeared onscreen together in the films “A Prairie Home Companion” and “Ricki and the Flash.”

articles.title: MS NOW Hosts ‘Disappointed’ Management Has Yet to Reach WGA Union Deal Guaranteeing ‘Fair Wages’; Network Boss Rebecca Kutler Responds to Accusations
articles.summary: Rachel Maddow and more than a dozen other MS NOW on-air hosts issued a public letter urging parent company Versant Media to reach a new deal with unionized employees affiliated with WGA East that ensures “fair wages and protections,” before their previous agreement expires Dec. 3.
body: Writers Guild of America East members at MS NOW are currently negotiating for a second collective bargaining agreement. “Despite the network’s historic midterm ratings and strong performance across the business, workers are still fighting for a fair contract with Versant Media Group management,” the union said.

MS NOW hosts and guests including Rachel Maddow, Jen Psaki, Christopher Hayes, Lawrence O’Donnell and Nicolle Wallace signed onto “a letter of solidarity calling for a fair wages and protections for the MS NOW Union,” released Tuesday by WGA East. Others signing the letter included Ali Velshi, Amy McGrath, Alicia Menendez, Jacob Soboroff, David Noriega, Jillian Frankel, Ayman Mohyeldin, Katie Phang, Christine Jansing, Symone Sanders Townsend, Antonia Hylton, Jonathan Capehart and Michael Steele.

Kutler, who has led MS NOW since January 2025, addressed many of the allegations in a memo. “Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be,” she wrote.

articles.title: Catherine's cancer documentary makes me feel less alone, says Strictly's Amy Dowden
articles.summary: The dancer says Catherine's documentary about her cancer journey is "so important" to raise awareness.
body: Strictly Come Dancing's Amy Dowden says the upcoming documentary from Catherine, the Princess of Wales, about her cancer journey will help many people, including herself, "not feel so alone".
Dowden praised the documentary and said it confirmed how "anyone can be dealt the devastating blow of a cancer diagnosis".
Dowden, Strictly's first Welsh professional dancer, was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer at 32 and has undergone chemotherapy and two mastectomies.
Catherine's BBC documentary, Heal, will reveal how cancer has impacted her outlook on life, as well as the people, places and experiences that have helped her.

articles.title: Francis Lawrence Signed On for One ‘Hunger Games’ Movie. Five Films Later, He’s the Keeper of Panem
articles.summary: The 'Sunrise on the Reaping' director looks back on the pressure of taking over a franchise, his decade-long collaboration with Suzanne Collins, why the series endures, and where things stand on ‘Constantine 2’ and 'Red Rising.'
body: The morning after the New York premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence is still taking in the view from the night before.

“Last night at the premiere, for the first time, we had three generations of cast,” Lawrence tells The Hollywood Reporter of the Nov. 16 event. “There’s something really special about the time we’ve all spent together and the quality of people I’ve gotten to work with.”

Lawrence has been a constant across all of them. Since taking over from director Gary Ross with 2013’s Catching Fire, he has directed every Hunger Games film that followed, working alongside producer Nina Jacobson to turn Suzanne Collins’ dystopian saga following teenagers forced into fatal combat into one of Hollywood’s most dependable franchises. The original four films grossed roughly $2.98 billion worldwide, and Collins’ five books have sold more than 100 million copies globally, growing into one of the most successful young adult publishing franchises in history.

Still, the scale didn’t fully hit him until the final Mockingjay films. Around the release of the films, The Hunger Games: The Exhibition opened to fans, and Lawrence walked through it with his stars.

articles.title: BBC and Netflix team up for new CBeebies hub on streamer
articles.summary: The limited trial will see a CBeebies hub on Netflix for the first time and will feature 24 programmes.
body: The BBC and Netflix are to launch a trial hub on the streaming service next month, featuring 24 CBeebies shows.
Programmes including Hey Duggee, Numberblocks and Teletubbies can be seen on a branded CBeebies hub on Netflix from 2 December.
The trial's aim is to test new ways for the flagship pre-school channel to reach audiences. The BBC is the UK's largest commissioner of children's content.

BBC iPlayer will remain the home for all CBeebies content. Some CBeebies shows such as Shaun the Sheep are already available on Netflix, but this is the first time they will have a home hub on the subscription streamer.

articles.title: Disney Greenlights ‘Aquamarine’ Series Inspired by the 2006 Mermaid Movie; Emma Roberts to Reprise Role and Exec Produce
articles.summary: Kenzi Richardson stars in the live-action series. Along with Roberts, original star Jake McDorman and the film's director Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum also are on board.
body: Disney has greenlighted Aquamarine, a new live-action series inspired by the 2006 feature film.

Original stars Emma Roberts and Jake McDorman are reprising their roles from the cult classic and also serving as executive producers. Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum, who directed the original movie, directs the pilot and exec produces alongside Susan Cartsonis, who produced the film.

The cast also includes Briella Guiza (as Mia), Theodore Dalton (as August) and Annika Reese (as Paige). Roberts (who played Claire in the film) and McDorman (Raymond) reprise their roles from the film and serve as executive producers.

“ Aquamarine is a timeless coming-of-age story, and we’re excited to bring its humor, heart and sense of wonder to a new generation,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “At its core, it’s a story about the power of friendship, self-discovery and believing in yourself. And with a stellar cast led by Kenzi Richardson, there’s a magical quality to this story that I think audiences everywhere will really connect with.”
points: Along with Roberts, original star Jake McDorman and the film's director Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum also are on board.

articles.title: Bros announce first tour in a decade
articles.summary: The twins, from Camberley, will perform in 10-date tour in 2027 including at Wembley Arena.
body: Formed in Camberley, Surrey, in 1986 by twin brothers Matt and Luke Goss alongside Craig Logan, the band had hits including When Will I Be Famous?, Drop The Boy and I Owe You Nothing.
Logan left in 1989 and Bros split three years later, although Matt and Luke Goss reunited in 2017 and have not toured together since.
The 10-date tour in 2027 will include a Wembley Arena show, 38 years after Bros played to 77,000 fans at Wembley Stadium, where they became the youngest act to headline the venue at the age of 20.
The pair will perform across November and December in London, Portsmouth, Birmingham, Sheffield, Brighton, Bath, Derby, Glasgow, Newcastle and Manchester.

articles.title: “Alarming” Diversity Backtrack Happening In Film and TV Industry In Canada, Report Finds
articles.summary: Despite homegrown hits like 'Heated Rivalry' and 'North of North,' the Writers Guild of Canada warns “key barriers” to future work stand in the way of new diverse members joining its ranks.
body: As the Canadian film and TV industry remains committed to diversity, equity and inclusion, resisting pressures to backtrack in a post-Trump DEI rollback era, aspiring diverse screenwriters now find themselves struggling to advance in a shrinking business.
So says the Writers Guild of Canada in its latest Equity, Diversity and Inclusion report released on Tuesday.

While the guild pointed to more diverse screenwriters joining its Canadian ranks, WGC executive director Victoria Shen revealed in the report “alarming numbers that affect not only diverse writers, but all Canadian screenwriters. This is the second year in a row in which we saw a decline in the number of episodes across every production format covered by the report. While we have seen decreases in Canadian production in the past, these numbers demonstrate an industry in decline.”

The EDI report accounted for diverse writers in the WGC ranks by measuring the number of black, indigenous, LGBTQ2S, people of color and people with disabilities. And the percentage of diverse members in the WGC membership rose to 51 percent in 2025, up from 42 percent in 2024 and 33 percent in 2019.
